land.text: Xiazhou, Youzhou, Suizhou, Yinzhou and later Jingbian, granted to Tuoba Sigong in 881

predecessors.note: Tuoba Sigong, the senior Tangut leader at Xiazhou, had seized You Prefecture late in the Xianton era (861-874; 873 on the Western Xia page).

land.text: the Tangut state of Li Jiqian, named King of the Xia State by the Liao in 990 (Cliopatria's Western Xia row starts in 990)

successors.note: Li Jipeng surrendered the Dingnan Jiedushi to the Song in 982 (the four prefectures go to northern-song); his relative Li Jiqian refused to submit and carried the Tangut polity on.

land.text: the Dingnan Jiedushi, which Li Jipeng surrendered to the Song court in 982

successors.note: Held on paper until Li Jiqian's rising of 984-985.

capitals.name: Xiazhou (Hengshan, near Yulin)
capitals.note: The page puts the circuit's headquarters at modern Yulin; the point is the researcher's reading of Xiazhou (Tongwan, in Jingbian, is the later Great Xia capital). Not given as a coordinate on any page. Ends 981: Li Jipeng surrendered the Dingnan Jiedushi, Xiazhou included, to the Song in 982 (Western Xia page); no seat of Li Jiqian is located on the pages for 982-990 (reviewer ea-04-x).

correction.text: Xiazhou, Youzhou, Suizhou and Yinzhou (and later Jingbian), centred on modern Yulin in Shaanxi: the Dingnan Jiedushi, also known as Xiasui

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. 'Sigong was granted in 881 control of Xiazhou, Youzhou, Suizhou, Yinzhou, and later also Jingbian', the territory being called Dingnan Jiedushi, 'also known as Xiasui', centred on modern Yulin, Shaanxi. The 120 km circle (about 45,000 km2) is the researcher's reading; the pages give no area for these years (the infobox 800,000 and 1,000,000 km2 are for the Western Xia of the 11th and 12th centuries). Cliopatria's Western Xia row (990-1033, 113,513 km2) covers the Ordos and Helan, not this smaller block.

correction.text: Yinzhou, taken by Li Jiqian in 985

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe for 985-990 (982-984: nothing is drawn, since the four prefectures went to the Song in 982 and the pages place no holding of Li Jiqian before Yinzhou in 985; reviewer ea-04-x). After the 982 surrender the four prefectures were the Song's on paper; 'Jiqian captured Yinzhou' in 985 with large supplies and the page gives no other holding before the Liao title of 990. The Yinzhou circle (Mizhi, 60 km) is the researcher's reading; Li Jiqian's camp lay elsewhere in the Ordos and is not located on the pages.

region.text: Xiazhou, Youzhou, Suizhou and Yinzhou (and later Jingbian), centred on modern Yulin in Shaanxi: the Dingnan Jiedushi, also known as Xiasui

ledger.note: 881: the Tangut Tuoba clan gets the Dingnan Circuit. Tuoba Sigong, who had seized You Prefecture, 'was granted in 881 control of Xiazhou, Youzhou, Suizhou, Yinzhou, and later also Jingbian'; the Tuoba page has Xizong make him full military governor 'soon thereafter' and rename the circuit Dingnan, after he joined the coalition against Huang Chao.

region.text: Xiazhou, Youzhou, Suizhou and Yinzhou (and later Jingbian), centred on modern Yulin in Shaanxi: the Dingnan Jiedushi, also known as Xiasui

ledger.note: 982: Li Jipeng surrenders the Dingnan. 'Li Jipeng fled to the Song court and surrendered control of Dingnan Jiedushi'; his relative Li Jiqian refused to submit.

region.text: Yinzhou, taken by Li Jiqian in 985

ledger.note: 985: Li Jiqian takes Yinzhou. After the Song attack of 984 on his camp (his mother and wife were captured, he escaped), 'Jiqian captured Yinzhou the next year, along with large supplies'; from 986 he paid tribute to the Liao.

region.text: Yinzhou, the one holding the pages name in 985-990

ledger.note: 990: the Tangut state becomes the Xia. Li Jiqian 'accepted the title King of the Xia State' from the Liao emperor in 990 (infobox reign 990-1004); Cliopatria's Western Xia row begins here, and the Western Xia dossier should carry it on.

wars.name: Li Jiqian's rising against the Song

zones.text: Yinzhou, taken by Li Jiqian in 985

wars.outcome: Li Jiqian escaped the Song attack of 984, took Yinzhou in 985, paid tribute to the Liao from 986 and was named King of the Xia State in 990; the Song recognised him later (Li Jiqian page: Dingnan jiedushi 998-1004).
wars.note: After 982 the land is Song on paper and Li Jiqian's in fact; the Western Xia dossier carries it from 990.

certainty.note: The pages name four or five prefectures and a centre at Yulin but no frontier; the circle is a reading.

notes: New state (Cliopatria lacks the Dingnan; its Western Xia row starts in 990). No English Wikipedia page titled Dingnan Circuit was found (Dingnan_Circuit returned not found), so wikipedia is null. Open points: (1) the extent is a circle round Yulin, not a frontier; (2) the Dingnan is the same Tangut polity as the Western Xia, which the ea-05 dossier should list as successor via Li Jiqian (984-990, the Cliopatria row from 990); this dossier ends at the Liao title of 990 and carries 982-990 as a Song loss and the 985 gain of Yinzhou; (3) the Later Tang war on Xia Prefecture (933) and the Dingnan's tributary status are in other dossiers' ledgers; (4) the Tang dossier has no 881 loss to the Dingnan (the whole block is inside Cliopatria's Tang shape to 910).
